WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old", after Belshazzar was slain that night. Daniel 5:30–31
Daniel calls him "Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, which was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans". Daniel 9:1
He set 120 princes over the kingdom and three presidents over them, Daniel first, and "thought to set him over the whole realm". Daniel 6:1–3
When Daniel came out of the den unhurt, Darius wrote to "all people, nations, and languages" that men should "tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God". Daniel 6:25–27
"So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian." Daniel 6:28
The angel who speaks to Daniel says: "in the first year of Darius the Mede, even I, stood to confirm and to strengthen him." Daniel 11:1
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
He signed a decree forbidding prayer to any god but the king for thirty days, then later decreed that all should fear the God of Daniel. Daniel 6:7–9 Daniel 6:26
Daniel, "which is of the children of the captivity of Judah", was first of his three presidents. Daniel 6:2 Daniel 6:13

DATES DIFFER

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Daniel gives his age (about 62) and his first year, never a length of reign or a BC year.
KEIL (1872): FIRST YEAR 538 BC, TWO YEARS BEFORE CYRUS REIGNED ALONE
Keil counts Darius the Mede's first year over the Chaldean kingdom as 538 BC and deducts two years from Cyrus's nine at Babylon, so that Cyrus reigns alone from 536.
THE BABYLONIAN TABLETS (PARKER AND DUBBERSTEIN, 1942)
No years given[3]
Babylon fell on 13 October 539 BC; from then the Babylonian business tablets are dated by Cyrus. They give no year to a king Darius at this time.
Cyrus himself
the Greek (Theodotion) text of Bel and the Dragon, as reported by the Pulpit Commentary (1897)
The Greek addition to Daniel has Cyrus receive the kingdom where Daniel has Darius; the Pulpit Commentary notes that the two names could be confused in the Aramaic script of about 100 BC.[37]
Astyages
Eusebius, Chronicle (about AD 325), as reported by the Pulpit Commentary (1897)
Eusebius made Darius the Mede the last Median king, Astyages; the Pulpit Commentary finds nothing to support it.[37]
Gubaru (Gobryas), Cyrus's governor of Babylon
T. G. Pinches, as reported by the Pulpit Commentary (1897), which favours it; R. Dick Wilson (1915)

The Nabonidus Chronicle has Gobryas enter Babylon and Cyrus appoint him governor there, and Daniel's Darius "received" the kingdom and set princes over it. Wilson argues that a provincial ruler could be called "king" and that Daniel never calls Darius king of Media or Persia. Daniel 5:31 Daniel 9:1 [37][10][2]
Not a king known to history: a confusion in the tradition
S. R. Driver (1900); A. A. Bevan (as reported by the Pulpit Commentary, 1897), who took Darius son of Hystaspes to be meant

Driver holds that the records leave no room for a king between Babylon's capture and Cyrus's reign, and suggests the figure combines Gubaru with Darius son of Hystaspes. The Pulpit Commentary answers that Daniel 11 shows the writer knew the Persian kings came after Cyrus.[36][37]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say how long Darius the Mede reigned; Daniel mentions only his "first year".
Scripture does not say how he died, or how the kingdom passed to Cyrus; Daniel 6:28 names the two reigns one after the other.
Daniel never calls him king of Media or of Persia; he is "made king over the realm of the Chaldeans" (Dan 9:1).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textDaniel's Darius is kept apart from the Darius of Ezra, Haggai and Zechariah, whom Ezra calls "Darius king of Persia". Daniel calls this one "Darius the Median" and "Darius the Mede". Daniel 5:31 Daniel 11:1 Ezra 4:24

From the textDaniel names his father: "Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes". That Ahasuerus is named nowhere else and has his own person record, apart from the king of Esther. Daniel 9:1
Scholars' viewR. Dick Wilson (1915) took Daniel's Ahasuerus to be the Median king whom Herodotus calls Cyaxares; this is one reading among several. Daniel 9:1 [11]
